public_rationale: On 6 January 2026, Marcus wrote that he does not expect LeCun's world-model approach (JEPA), pursued at LeCun's new company, to solve many of the problems that have plagued LLMs. He gave no deadline. The forecast would be contradicted if public evaluations showed a JEPA-based or AMI Labs system largely fixing several core LLM problems, such as hallucination, reasoning reliability or generalization. It would be supported if no such result had appeared after a fair period. Before then, it can be settled in its favour only if the company abandons the approach. A Wikipedia summary, available by 1 October 2026, says AMI Labs is meant to remain a research organisation and is not expected to produce a saleable product for around five years (e1). The evidence gathered contains no public evaluation of JEPA-based or AMI Labs systems on these problems. It also contains no report of the approach being abandoned. A lack of results so far does not confirm the forecast, so it remains unresolved.
limitations: The only evidence is one secondary summary (e1) of AMI Labs' status and plans. It contains no technical results.
Not finding a public evaluation does not show that none exists.
'Many of the problems' is not quantified, so later evidence may be hard to score.
Marcus phrased this as an expectation, not a firm prediction.
This assessment does not judge the post's wider arguments about what a world model needs.
